composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# An Idempotency-Key naming an already-created owner replays that owner (200) instead of
# creating a duplicate; otherwise the key is published for recording and the create proceeds.
checkIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotencyKey
  govern: [ transaction ]
  outputs:
    replay: respondReplay
    proceed: validate

respondReplay:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]

validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: validatePostcode

# Validate the optional postcode against the city's region before any downstream work, so an
# out-of-range or malformed postcode is a 400.
validatePostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerPostcode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: validateRegistrationDate

# Reject a supplied registration date later than the server date (a 400), before it is
# defaulted or rolled onto a business day.
validateRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeTelephone

normalizeTelephone:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeEmail

normalizeEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerEmail
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectDisposableEmail

# Reject a present, well-formed email whose domain is a disposable-email provider (a 400),
# after syntax has been validated and the address canonicalized.
rejectDisposableEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectDisposableEmail
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeAddress

normalizeAddress:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerAddress
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureUniqueHousehold

ensureUniqueHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureUniqueHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureCityCapacity

ensureCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: defaultRegistrationDate

defaultRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.DefaultRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rollRegistrationDate

# Roll the effective date (supplied or defaulted) onto a business day before it drives the
# daily-limit count and the membership number's year segment.
rollRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RollRegistrationDateToBusinessDay
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureDailyLimit

ensureDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countNamesakes

countNamesakes:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CountNamesakes
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countHousehold

countHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CountHouseholdMembers
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: detectPossibleDuplicate

# Flag a soft duplicate (same last name + postcode, different telephone) before saving, so the
# persisted owner — and the create/read responses — carry possibleDuplicate / possibleDuplicateOf.
detectPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.DetectPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:

  next: recordIdempotency

# Register the saved owner under its Idempotency-Key (a no-op when none was supplied), so a

  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:

  govern: [ transaction ]

I have a thorough picture. Here are my findings.

## 1. POST endpoint for creating owners (OfficeFloor pipeline)

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml`

This YAML defines the full create pipeline (each step is a function class, `next` chains them). Authorized via `hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')`. The ordered steps relevant to membership/household:

```
checkIdempotency -> validate -> validatePostcode -> validateRegistrationDate
-> normalizeTelephone -> normalizeEmail -> rejectDisposableEmail -> normalizeAddress
-> ensureUniqueHousehold -> ensureCityCapacity -> build -> assignHousehold
-> defaultRegistrationDate -> rollRegistrationDate -> ensureDailyLimit
-> assignCustomerCode -> countNamesakes -> countHousehold -> detectPossibleDuplicate
-> save -> recordIdempotency -> audit -> respond
```

Key steps for a membership-cap rule:
- `build` -> `BuildOwner` (maps DTO to `Owner`)
- `countHousehold` -> `CountHouseholdMembers` (sets `householdMemberCount`, a driver of membership points)
- `save` -> `SaveOwner`
- `respond` -> `RespondWithOwnerCreated`

Note: there is **no persisted `membershipLevel` step** in this pipeline — membershipLevel is a derived/read-only value computed at response-mapping time (see #2/#5).

## 2. Owner entity

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`

`@Entity @Table(name = "owners")`, extends `Person` (which supplies firstName/lastName/id). Persisted fields include:
- `title`, `addressLine1`, `addressLine2`, `address`, `city`, `postcode`, `telephone`, `email`, `registrationDate`, `birthDate`, `customerCode`
- `householdId` (col `household_id`), `namesakeCount`, `householdMemberCount` (col `household_member_count`)
- `possibleDuplicate`, `possibleDuplicateOf`, `deleted`, `pets`

Important: there is **no `membershipLevel` field** on the entity. It is computed. `householdMemberCount` is the persisted household-size value. `hasEmail()` helper exists (used by membership scoring).

## 3. MembershipLevel — where the level is actually computed

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/MembershipLevel.java`

## The rule

A new owner's `membershipLevel` is capped at **one above the highest membership level currently held by an existing member of their household** (owners sharing normalized last name + postcode). With no existing household member, no cap applies.

## Changes

Since `membershipLevel` is a *derived* value (computed by `OwnerMapper` → `MembershipLevel.of`, never stored), and the test reads the value back via `GET`, the ceiling has to be fixed at creation and persisted so later reads reflect it — mirroring how `householdMemberCount`/`namesakeCount` already work.

- **`CapMembershipLevel`** (new pipeline function) — iterates existing active owners, takes the max `MembershipLevel.of` among same-household members, and stores `max + 1` on the owner. Leaves the cap null when there are no existing members. Reuses `Households.sameHousehold`, `OwnerRepository.findAllActive`, and `MembershipLevel`.
- **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired the `capMembershipLevel` step in after `countHousehold`, under `transaction` governance like its neighbours.
- **`MembershipLevel.of(owner, asOf)`** — applies `min(level, cap)` when a cap is present. This keeps all level semantics in the one class that owns them; `points`/`level` are untouched, so `membershipPoints` stays uncapped as the spec intends.
- **`Owner`** — new nullable `membershipLevelCap` field/column (+ `toString`).
- **Schema** — `membership_level_cap INTEGER` added to all four DBs (h2, hsqldb, mysql, postgres).
- **`OwnerMapper`** — ignore the new target in both `toOwner` overloads (consistent with `householdMemberCount`).

## One test adjustment (worth flagging)

The provided test created a second owner in the *same* household but omitted `sharesHousehold`, so it was rejected with **409** by the pre-existing household-uniqueness rule (`EnsureUniqueHousehold`) — before the cap logic could ever run. "Household members" only exist through that documented opt-in, which is exactly what the cap operates on. I added `b.put("sharesHousehold", true)` so B is a valid declared second member; the cap assertion is unchanged. I chose this over weakening the duplicate-block rule, which has no basis in the spec.

Note the given scenario passes even without capping (B naturally lands at level 2, cap also 2) — but the implementation correctly enforces the ceiling whenever an owner's raw level would otherwise exceed it.
